X.label: X axis
X.description: Target position on the X axis. The control writes the sign, and an I in front of the word makes the value incremental.

Y.label: Y axis
Y.description: Target position on the Y axis. An I in front of the word makes the value incremental.

Z.label: Z axis
Z.description: Target position on the Z axis. An I in front of the word makes the value incremental.

U.label: U axis
U.description: Extra linear axis parallel to X.

V.label: V axis
V.description: Extra linear axis parallel to Y.

W.label: W axis
W.description: Extra linear axis parallel to Z.

PR.label: Polar radius
PR.description: Distance of the point from the pole that CC set.

PA.label: Polar angle
PA.description: Angle of the point around the pole that CC set.

CCA.label: Opening angle
CCA.description: Angle of the arc in an approach or departure block.

R.label: Radius
R.description: Radius value, for instance of a CR arc, an RND rounding or a tool definition.

DR.label: Direction of rotation, or radius oversize
DR.description: In an arc block it gives the direction: DR+ counter-clockwise, DR- clockwise. In a tool call a number follows and it is the radius oversize of the tool.

DR2.label: Corner radius oversize
DR2.description: Oversize on the corner radius of the tool, added to the value in the tool table.

DL.label: Length oversize
DL.description: Oversize on the length of the tool, added to the value in the tool table.

F.label: Feed
F.description: Feed rate. The unit follows the program header: millimetres per minute in an MM program, tenths of an inch per minute in an INCH program, and degrees per minute on a rotary axis. FMAX means rapid and FAUTO takes the feed from the last tool call.

FU.label: Feed per revolution
FU.description: Feed given as distance per spindle revolution.

FZ.label: Feed per tooth
FZ.description: Feed given as distance per cutting edge.

S.label: Spindle speed
S.description: Spindle speed in revolutions per minute.

M.label: Miscellaneous function
M.description: Switches a machine function such as spindle or coolant. A block may carry up to four of them.

Q.label: Q parameter, global
Q.description: Numbered variable shared by the whole program and by the programs it calls.

QL.label: Q parameter, local
QL.description: Numbered variable that is valid only inside the program it is used in.

QR.label: Q parameter, persistent
QR.description: Numbered variable that keeps its value after the program ends.

QS.label: Q parameter, string
QS.description: Variable that holds text rather than a number, for instance a tool or program name.

NX.label: Surface normal X
NX.description: X part of the surface normal vector in an LN block. CAM writes all three parts.

NY.label: Surface normal Y
NY.description: Y part of the surface normal vector in an LN block. CAM writes all three parts.

NZ.label: Surface normal Z
NZ.description: Z part of the surface normal vector in an LN block. CAM writes all three parts.

TX.label: Tool vector X
TX.description: X part of the tool orientation vector in an LN block. It is always a number, never a Q parameter.

TY.label: Tool vector Y
TY.description: Y part of the tool orientation vector in an LN block. It is always a number, never a Q parameter.

TZ.label: Tool vector Z
TZ.description: Z part of the tool orientation vector in an LN block. It is always a number, never a Q parameter.

LEN.label: Approach length
LEN.description: Length of the straight part of an approach or departure move.

MB.label: Retract distance
MB.description: How far to pull back along the tool axis with M140. MB MAX goes to the travel limit.

REP.label: Repeat count
REP.description: How many extra times a label section is run.

codes.label: Program start
codes.description: First block of a program. It carries the program name and the unit the program is written in, MM or INCH.

codes.label: Program end
codes.description: Last block of a program. Name and unit repeat what the start block says.

codes.label: Millimetre program
codes.description: The program is written in millimetres: coordinates in mm and a feed in mm per minute. It stands in the start and the end block, and both have to say the same.

codes.label: Inch program
codes.description: The program is written in inches: coordinates in inch and a feed in tenths of an inch per minute, so F100 is ten inches per minute.

codes.label: Stock definition
codes.description: Describes the raw part for the graphics. Sub-block 0.1 carries the tool axis and one corner, sub-block 0.2 the opposite corner.

codes.label: Tool call
codes.description: Changes to the tool given as a number, a name in quotes or a QS parameter, sets the tool axis and the speed, and switches the length compensation on. A tool call without a tool argument only changes speed or feed and is not a tool change.

codes.label: Tool definition or pre-selection
codes.description: After a tool call it stages the next tool in the magazine, which is machine dependent. With L and R values it defines the tool geometry inside the program.

codes.label: Straight line
codes.description: Straight move to the end point. Axes that are not written keep their last value. The block may also carry the radius compensation, a feed and M functions.

codes.label: Circle centre
codes.description: Sets the circle centre, also called the pole, for the arc blocks that follow. It makes no motion and stays until the next CC.

codes.label: Arc around the centre
codes.description: Arc to the end point around the last CC, turning in the direction that DR gives. An end point equal to the start point makes a full circle.

codes.label: Arc by radius
codes.description: Arc to the end point with the radius R. A positive R takes the arc shorter than half a circle, a negative R the longer one; DR gives the direction. The chord cannot be longer than the diameter.

codes.label: Tangential arc
codes.description: Arc to the end point that joins the previous contour element smoothly. It needs at least two positioned blocks before it.

codes.label: Corner rounding
codes.description: Rounds the corner between the previous and the next contour element. A feed in this block applies to the rounding only.

codes.label: Chamfer
codes.description: Cuts a chamfer of the given length between two straight elements. It cannot be the first block of a contour, and a feed in this block applies to the chamfer only.

codes.label: Straight line, polar
codes.description: Straight line given around the pole set with CC: PR is the radius, PA the angle, and IPR or IPA make them incremental.

codes.label: Arc around the pole, polar
codes.description: Arc around the pole set with CC, given by the angle PA and the direction DR. With an incremental total angle and a height in the tool axis it becomes a helix.

codes.label: Tangential arc, polar
codes.description: Arc that leaves the previous element tangentially and ends at a polar point, given by PR and PA.

codes.label: Straight line with a surface normal
codes.description: Straight line that also carries the direction of the surface: X, Y and Z give the end point, NX, NY and NZ the normal, and TX, TY and TZ the tool orientation. The control uses them for three-dimensional compensation.

codes.label: Approach on a tangential line
codes.description: Moves onto the first contour point along a straight line that leaves the contour tangentially. LEN gives the length of that line.

codes.label: Approach on a normal line
codes.description: Moves onto the first contour point along a straight line at a right angle to the contour. LEN gives the length of that line.

codes.label: Approach on a tangential arc
codes.description: Moves onto the first contour point along an arc that meets the contour tangentially, given by its radius R and the centre angle CCA.

codes.label: Approach on a line and a tangential arc
codes.description: Moves onto the first contour point along a straight line followed by an arc that meets the contour tangentially.

codes.label: Depart on a tangential line
codes.description: Leaves the last contour point along a straight line that continues the contour tangentially, and cancels the radius compensation.

codes.label: Depart on a normal line
codes.description: Leaves the last contour point along a straight line at a right angle to the contour, and cancels the radius compensation.

codes.label: Depart on a tangential arc
codes.description: Leaves the last contour point along an arc that continues the contour tangentially, and cancels the radius compensation.

codes.label: Depart on an arc and a line
codes.description: Leaves the last contour point along a tangential arc followed by a straight line, and cancels the radius compensation.

codes.label: No radius compensation
codes.description: The centre of the tool follows the programmed path. CAM output usually works this way.

codes.label: Radius compensation, left
codes.description: Puts the tool to the left of the contour seen in the direction of travel. Go through an R0 block before switching to the other side, and do not switch it on in an arc.

codes.label: Radius compensation, right
codes.description: Puts the tool to the right of the contour seen in the direction of travel. Go through an R0 block before switching to the other side, and do not switch it on in an arc.

codes.label: Rapid
codes.description: Moves at rapid speed. It counts for this block only; afterwards the last numeric feed applies again.

codes.label: Feed from the tool call
codes.description: Uses the feed that was written in the last tool call.

codes.label: Label
codes.description: Marks a jump target, given as a number or a name in quotes. LBL 0 marks the end of a subprogram and may appear many times; every other label may be set once.

codes.label: Call label
codes.description: Runs the section from that label up to the next LBL 0 and then carries on. REP runs the section that many extra times.

codes.label: Call program
codes.description: Runs another program as a subprogram. The called program must not contain M2 or M30, Q parameters stay shared, and active transformations stay on after the call.

codes.label: Select a program
codes.description: Names the program that a later CALL SELECTED PGM block runs, so the path can be put together while the program runs.

codes.label: Repeat a label section
codes.description: Repeat count behind CALL LBL: the section between the label and the call runs this many times more, so REP 4 runs it five times altogether.

codes.label: Q parameter function
codes.description: Calculates with Q parameters. FN 0 assigns, FN 1 to FN 4 add, subtract, multiply and divide, FN 5 to FN 8 are square root, sine, cosine and the root of a sum of squares, and FN 9 upwards jump to a label when a comparison holds.

codes.label: Cycle definition
codes.description: Defines a cycle and stores its values. An old-style cycle up to number 39 is written as CYCL DEF <number>.<sub> over several numbered blocks; a cycle from 200 upwards is a header line plus one indented line per Q parameter, and every line but the last ends in a continuation mark.

codes.label: Tolerance cycle
codes.description: Sets how far the path may leave the programmed contour, which is what decides accuracy against speed on a fast contour. It is written in numbered sub-blocks: 32.0 carries the name, 32.1 the tolerance T in millimetres, and 32.2 the HSC-MODE, 0 for accuracy and 1 for speed, together with TA for the rotary axes.

codes.label: Cycle call
codes.description: Runs the cycle that was defined last at the current position. CYCL CALL PAT runs it at every point of a preceding pattern definition.

codes.label: Cycle call on a pattern
codes.description: Runs the cycle that was defined last at every point of the PATTERN DEF or the point table in front of it.

codes.label: Cycle call at a position
codes.description: Moves to the position written in the block and runs the cycle that was defined last there.

codes.label: Drilling cycle
codes.description: Drills to depth, in pecks when an infeed is given, and pulls back fully between the pecks. It pre-positions in the tool axis itself.

params.label: Dwell at the top after each retract
Workpiece surface in the tool axis
Depth reference: 0 tool tip, 1 full diameter

codes.label: Reaming cycle
codes.description: Feeds down to depth and feeds back out again, so the reamer leaves a clean wall.

params.label: Workpiece surface in the tool axis

codes.label: Universal drilling cycle
codes.description: Drills to depth with pecks that get shorter as the hole deepens and with chip breaks in between.

params.label: Dwell at the top after each retract
Workpiece surface in the tool axis
How much shorter each peck gets
Retract distance for a chip break
Depth reference: 0 tool tip, 1 full diameter

codes.label: Universal deep-hole drilling cycle
codes.description: Drills deep holes with shortening pecks, chip breaks and a controlled return into the hole.

params.label: Workpiece surface in the tool axis
How much shorter each peck gets
Upper stop distance for the fast return
Lower stop distance for the fast return
Retract distance for a chip break
Depth reference: 0 tool tip, 1 full diameter

codes.label: Tapping cycle with a floating holder
codes.description: Cuts a thread with a compensating chuck. The plunging feed follows from the speed and the thread pitch, so scaling it would change the thread.

params.label: Thread depth, negative into the material
Plunging feed from speed times pitch
Workpiece surface in the tool axis

codes.label: Rigid tapping cycle
codes.description: Cuts a thread without a compensating chuck: the control keeps the spindle and the feed in step from the pitch. The sign of the pitch decides right- or left-hand.

params.label: Thread depth, negative into the material
Workpiece surface in the tool axis

codes.label: Rigid tapping cycle with chip breaking
codes.description: Cuts a thread without a compensating chuck and pulls back now and then to break the chip.

params.label: Thread depth, negative into the material
Workpiece surface in the tool axis
Retract distance for a chip break

codes.label: Centring cycle
codes.description: Spots a hole, either down to a depth or until the cone reaches a given diameter.

params.label: Mode: 0 to a depth, 1 to a diameter
Workpiece surface in the tool axis

codes.label: Tilt the working plane by spatial angles
codes.description: Turns the working plane by three angles around the machine axes. All three are written even when one is zero, and a following word says whether the machine swivels with a compensating move, turns the rotary axes only, or stays put.

codes.label: Reset the tilted working plane
codes.description: Switches the tilted plane off again. Use it rather than writing zero angles.

codes.label: Tool centre point management on
codes.description: Keeps the tool tip on the programmed path while the rotary axes move, and says how the feed and the rotary positions are read.

codes.label: Tool centre point management off
codes.description: Switches tool centre point management off again.

codes.label: Program stop
codes.description: Stops the program at the end of the block. Whether spindle and coolant stop with it depends on the machine.

codes.label: Optional stop
codes.description: Stops the program only while the operator has the optional-stop switch on.

codes.label: Programmed stop
codes.description: Stops the program at the end of this block until the operator presses start again. An M function may stand in the same block.

codes.label: Program end
codes.description: Ends the program at the end of the block. Subprograms go after it.

codes.label: Program end
codes.description: Ends the program at the end of the block, the same as M2.

codes.label: Spindle on, clockwise
codes.description: Starts the spindle clockwise at the start of the block.

codes.label: Spindle on, counter-clockwise
codes.description: Starts the spindle counter-clockwise at the start of the block.

codes.label: Spindle stop
codes.description: Stops the spindle at the end of the block.

codes.label: Tool change
codes.description: Machine-dependent tool change. In Klartext the change itself is done by the tool call, so M6 is not what marks a new tool.

codes.label: Coolant on
codes.description: Turns the coolant on at the start of the block.

codes.label: Coolant off
codes.description: Turns the coolant off at the end of the block.

codes.label: Spindle clockwise and coolant on
codes.description: Starts the spindle clockwise and the coolant in one go.

codes.label: Spindle counter-clockwise and coolant on
codes.description: Starts the spindle counter-clockwise and the coolant in one go.

codes.label: Modal cycle call
codes.description: Calls the cycle that was defined last as a modal call. What exactly it does is machine dependent.

codes.label: Machine coordinates for this block
codes.description: The positions in this block are read from the machine datum, and the tool length is not applied. It counts for this block only.

codes.label: Builder reference point for this block
codes.description: The positions in this block are read from a reference point that the machine builder set. It counts for this block only.

codes.label: Reduce the rotary axis display
codes.description: Brings the displayed value of a rotary axis back below a full turn.

codes.label: Datum shift
codes.description: Shifts the datum without a cycle: TRANS DATUM AXIS takes the shift from the axis values in the block, TRANS DATUM TABLE takes a line of the datum table, and TRANS DATUM RESET cancels the shift.

codes.label: Call the cycle once
codes.description: Runs the last defined cycle once at the end position of this block. It counts for this block only.

codes.label: Rotary feed in millimetres per minute
codes.description: Reads the feed of a rotary axis as a path speed rather than an angular speed.

codes.label: Rotary feed in millimetres per minute off
codes.description: Takes back M116.

codes.label: Shortest path for rotary axes
codes.description: Moves a rotary axis the short way round to the programmed angle.

codes.label: Shortest path for rotary axes off
codes.description: Takes back M126.

codes.label: Keep the tool tip on the path
codes.description: Holds the tool tip on the programmed position while tilt axes move. Switch it off before a tool call or a machine-coordinate block. An F in the block sets the feed of the compensating moves.

codes.label: Keep the tool tip on the path off
codes.description: Takes back M128 at the end of the block.

codes.label: Retract along the tool axis
codes.description: Pulls the tool back along its own axis by the distance after MB, or to the travel limit with MB MAX. It counts for this block only.
